outputs.justify_why_test_is_missing: This panel consists of a diagram and images of western blots with no quantitative comparison needing statistical tests.
Quantitative comparisons of percent HTT depletion and elution abundance require statistical validation to ensure the differences are significant.
The heatmap represents quantitative data subjected to clustering and should include statistical measures to support the selection and differentiation of clusters.
Violin plots typically represent distributions that should be analyzed with statistical tests to understand differences between groups.
Bar plots with error bars suggest group comparisons that require statistical tests to verify differences in protein levels are significant.
This panel displays sequence alignment and structural predictions, which are qualitative analyses that do not require statistical tests.
Scatter plots showing correlations should provide statistical analysis to validate the strength and significance of the observed relationships.
While a correlation coefficient (R^2) is provided, additional statistical tests should confirm the significance of the correlation.
PCA plots visually suggest variance, but statistical validation of PCA components' significance is needed to support the data interpretation.
Like panel I, PCA plots should be accompanied by statistical validation to confirm the significance of differences between groups.
